transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-03-25
- Start: 09:30 AM PT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia M., Darren L., Priya N., Ethan Z., Amir H., Lena P., Matteo R., Janelle C., Marcus G., Olivia C.

Summary: Quick sync to hand off Q2 roadmap activities and ensure launch readiness for the next model rollout. Also a short incident review of last week's canary flakiness and action items for stability.

Topics: roadmap priorities, launch checklist, canary incident, capacity/resourcing, observability needs, security signoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Alright everyone, uh thanks for joining, let's, um, kick off. The goal today is to finalize owners for the launch checklist and walk through the incident from last week so we don't repeat it.
[00:15] Lena Park: Yep, high level — we want product signoff this week and a controlled canary next week. Depend on SRE and platform to set windows.
[00:32] Darren Lee: Quick add, engineering is about 80% done with the batching/kv cache changes; there's one perf regress we need to mitigate.
[00:45] Ethan Zhao: Right, the regress showed up under long-tail sequences in the canary; we saw increased latency during cache miss storms, likely around the KV eviction path.
[01:03] Amir Haddad: We're seeing a pattern where prefix cache invalidation causes extra work across pods, the routing layer then falls back to a lower capacity pool and that amplifies latency — we have a mitigation in testing.
[01:22] Janelle Cruz: From QA — the regression surfaced in two tests: end-to-end streaming and multi-tenant isolation; I have logs but some names are garbled in the transcript, I'll attach in doc.
[01:40] Sofia Martinez: Ok, so immediate ask: Ethan and Amir, can you run a focused canary with the mitigation and a smaller traffic profile?
[01:52] Ethan Zhao: Yeah, we'll spin a canary and throttle to 10% with synthetic traffic that mirrors long-seq tails. Need permission to bump some infra just for that window.
[02:06] Matteo Rossi: Fine, but keep cost/time in mind; we don't want unnecessary bursts. Also we need a clear SLO target to judge success.
[02:19] Priya Nair: I'll coordinate the calendar and stakeholders; we should notify support, sales and docs ahead of the canary.
[02:33] Olivia Chen: Support here — please include runbooks and expected failure modes so we can triage quickly.
[02:45] Marcus Green: Security note — ensure the KMS keys are rotated as per the recent policy, and audit logs are preserved for the canary.
[02:59] Sofia Martinez: Good call. On the roadmap side, we have three launch pillars: performance (batching + kv fixes), observability (console dashboards + traces), and resilience (fallback model variants + routing policies).
[03:20] Darren Lee: For performance, timeline is: internal perf fixes by 3/27, extended benching 3/28-3/30, then canary 4/1-4/3.
[03:34] Janelle Cruz: QA timeline aligned, we'll start smoke tests 3/29 and full reg tests 3/30-3/31.
[03:45] Lena Park: Product needs to own rollout criteria: no P0s in canary; less than 1.5x latency increase at p95, errors under 0.5% for core generation routes.
[03:59] Ethan Zhao: Those are reasonable, we'll instrument p95/p99 and error rates and share dashboards.
[04:12] Amir Haddad: On observability, we need per-route token-level cost breakdown available in Console before launch; current ETA is 3/28 to wire up new metrics.
[04:26] Priya Nair: That ties into ops communications — I'll update runbook links with the Console dashboard once it's live.
[04:40] Janelle Cruz: Incident review quick notes: root cause seems to be an interaction between the new KV eviction heuristic and routing fallback under small cluster sizes. Logs show cascading retries.
[04:58] Darren Lee: Action there is to add a short-circuit in eviction and increase the quorum threshold during high load. We'll patch and test.
[05:12] Matteo Rossi: Also we should consider a config guardrail: auto-disabled aggressive eviction during canary windows.
[05:23] Amir Haddad: Agreed, we can add a runtime flag to disable eviction policy. It's low risk and easy to toggle.
[05:36] Sofia Martinez: Ok, owners — Darren + Amir to ship the patch; Ethan to run canary; Janelle to validate; Marcus to confirm security gating.
[05:49] Marcus Green: I'll verify KMS/HSM usage and ensure that audit logs are forwarded; if anything looks off we'll pause.
[06:02] Sofia Martinez: On communications, Priya pinged the cross-functional list; please don't assume it's internal only — include sales for dedicated customers.
[06:14] Olivia Chen: Noted. We'll prepare a short customer-facing note if we see any impact.
[06:27] Priya Nair: Resourcing note — we might need an extra infra engineer for the first 48 hours of canary to triage. Darren, can we borrow one?
[06:38] Darren Lee: We can, I can reassign Rohit for the window, he'll focus on KV/routing.
[06:48] Sofia Martinez: Great. A few Q&A style exchanges then wrap: (crosstalk)
[06:55] Janelle Cruz: Quick question — what's the rollback plan if canary fails?
[07:02] Ethan Zhao: Rollback is immediate to previous model variant with traffic cut by 80% and a staged rollback for stateful caches; we have a script but will test it during dry run.
[07:21] Matteo Rossi: Ensure DB migrations or model cache warmups are reversible or avoided during canary.
[07:34] Priya Nair: I'll schedule a dry run 3/30 where we flip traffic in a simulated window, confirm rollback works.
[07:45] Sofia Martinez: Perfect. Anything else on launch readiness?
[07:50] Lena Park: One ask — product wants a short checklist item for compliance: SOC2 artifacts updated and golden config in repo.
[07:59] Marcus Green: I'll confirm SOC2 artifact location and add a ticket to update docs.
[08:08] Sofia Martinez: Wrap-up — recap next steps and owners.
[08:13] (brief recap)
[08:20] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in doc and execute.

Notes: transcript contains small transcription errors (names occasionally abbreviated); attachments referenced: perf logs, canary runbook, QA test matrix. Links to be shared in follow-up doc.
